notes:
On Windows, a chapter that both machines had changed could disappear from the binder after a sync. Its text was never lost: it sat in the chapter's folder under a name ending in “.conflict1”, which Corylus did not recognise. Corylus now keeps the chapter in its place, holding this computer's version, while you decide between the two. If one version simply continues the other, it picks the newer one on its own. A chapter already affected is put back automatically on your next sync.

- A sync that stops responding is now cancelled rather than left running in the background. A stuck sync could carry on uploading unnoticed and hold up every sync after it, and that is how a normal edit could end up reported as a conflict.
